================================================================================
EXAMPLE 07: MULTI-UNIT HYDROPOWER PLANT WITH AGC
================================================================================

This example demonstrates automatic generation control (AGC)
for a multi-unit hydropower plant with:
  - 3 units: 100 MW, 120 MW, 150 MW
  - Primary frequency control (governor droop)
  - Secondary frequency control (AGC)
  - Economic dispatch and unit commitment

================================================================================
SCENARIO 1: FREQUENCY DISTURBANCE RESPONSE
================================================================================

A large load is added to the grid at t=10s, causing frequency to drop.
The hydropower plant must respond with:
  - Primary control: Immediate power increase via governor droop
  - Secondary control: AGC eliminates steady-state frequency error

Initial Conditions:
  Plant demand: 250.0 MW
  System frequency: 50.0 Hz
  Tie-line flow: 0.0 MW (scheduled: 0.0 MW)


================================================================================
RESULTS ANALYSIS
================================================================================

Initial State (t=0-10s):
  Total generation: 250.00 MW
    Unit 1: 67.57 MW
    Unit 2: 81.08 MW
    Unit 3: 101.35 MW

Peak Response (t=11-15s):
  Maximum generation: 332.50 MW
  Power increase: 82.50 MW

Final State (t=50-60s):
  Total generation: 92.50 MW
  Average frequency: 50.000 Hz
  Frequency error: 0.0 mHz
    Unit 1: 25.00 MW
    Unit 2: 30.00 MW
    Unit 3: 37.50 MW

Performance Metrics:
  ACE standard deviation (final): 0.00 MW
  Frequency restored: Yes

Plot saved: scenario1_frequency_disturbance.png

================================================================================
SCENARIO 2: LOAD VARIATION AND UNIT COMMITMENT
================================================================================

Plant load varies from 50 MW to 320 MW over 2 minutes.
Units are committed and decommitted based on load.

Load Profile:
  t=0-20s:   50 MW (1 unit)
  t=20-40s:  80-180 MW (ramping, 2-3 units)
  t=40-60s:  180-260 MW (ramping, 3 units)
  t=60-80s:  260 MW (3 units at high load)
  t=80-100s: 260-180 MW (ramping down)
  t=100-120s: 180 MW (3 units)


================================================================================
RESULTS ANALYSIS
================================================================================

Unit Commitment at Key Time Points:

t=10s: Demand=50.0 MW, Committed Units=1
  Unit 1: OFF
  Unit 2: OFF
  Unit 3: 50.0 MW (33.3% of capacity)

t=30s: Demand=130.0 MW, Committed Units=3
  Unit 1: 35.1 MW (35.1% of capacity)
  Unit 2: 42.2 MW (35.1% of capacity)
  Unit 3: 52.7 MW (35.1% of capacity)

t=50s: Demand=220.0 MW, Committed Units=3
  Unit 1: 59.5 MW (59.5% of capacity)
  Unit 2: 71.4 MW (59.5% of capacity)
  Unit 3: 89.2 MW (59.5% of capacity)

t=70s: Demand=260.0 MW, Committed Units=3
  Unit 1: 70.3 MW (70.3% of capacity)
  Unit 2: 84.3 MW (70.3% of capacity)
  Unit 3: 105.4 MW (70.3% of capacity)

t=90s: Demand=220.0 MW, Committed Units=3
  Unit 1: 59.5 MW (59.5% of capacity)
  Unit 2: 71.4 MW (59.5% of capacity)
  Unit 3: 89.2 MW (59.5% of capacity)

t=110s: Demand=180.0 MW, Committed Units=3
  Unit 1: 48.6 MW (48.6% of capacity)
  Unit 2: 58.4 MW (48.6% of capacity)
  Unit 3: 73.0 MW (48.6% of capacity)

Plot saved: scenario2_load_variation.png

================================================================================
SCENARIO 3: TIE-LINE POWER CONTROL
================================================================================

Scheduled tie-line export changes from 0 MW to 50 MW at t=30s.
AGC must increase generation to maintain tie-line schedule.

Initial Conditions:
  Plant demand: 200.0 MW
  Tie-line scheduled: 0 MW -> 50 MW at t=30s


================================================================================
RESULTS ANALYSIS
================================================================================

Before Schedule Change (t=20-30s):
  Generation: 200.00 MW
  Tie-line flow: 0.00 MW

After Schedule Change (t=70-90s):
  Generation: 92.50 MW
  Tie-line flow: -107.40 MW
  Generation increase: -107.50 MW

Plot saved: scenario3_tie_line_control.png

================================================================================
ALL SCENARIOS COMPLETED
================================================================================

Key Findings:
   Primary control provides immediate frequency response
   Secondary control (AGC) eliminates steady-state errors
   Load allocation optimizes efficiency across units
   Unit commitment adapts to load variations
   Tie-line power control maintains scheduled exchanges

The integrated AGC system successfully coordinates multiple
generating units while maintaining frequency and tie-line schedules.
